answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. It resists because the per-account limit caps any single farm, spreading the surplus across many passing identities instead of letting one cluster monopolize it. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a ripple as the anchor of the cost.
